messages.content: I need to work out Atlanta flights before we look at the hotel. The district review is Monday, December 7 at 1:30 p.m. in Buckhead, and I have a restaurant visit Tuesday morning in Sandy Springs.
What window is set for the Tuesday visit, and are you considering Sunday night as well as Monday morning for the outbound?

The visit is 9:00 to 11:00 a.m. Tuesday. Compare a reasonable Sunday evening nonstop with a Monday morning nonstop. For the return, show me an early afternoon option and an evening one. Don’t book anything yet.

I found two nonstop outbound options from O’Hare. Sunday, December 6: depart 6:10 p.m., arrive Atlanta 9:12 p.m. Monday, December 7: depart 7:00 a.m., arrive 10:03 a.m. The Sunday flight adds a hotel night but removes the same-day arrival risk. The Monday flight leaves 3 hours 27 minutes between scheduled arrival and the review.
How much of that Monday margin disappears getting to Buckhead? The review is at our support center near Lenox Square.

From ATL to the Lenox Square area, allow roughly 35 to 55 minutes by car in late-morning traffic, plus about 20 to 30 minutes to deplane and reach the pickup area. With an on-time 10:03 arrival, you would likely reach the support center around 11:00 to 11:30. That leaves about two hours before the 1:30 review, but a delay of an hour would make the margin noticeably thinner.
That is workable. What are the Tuesday returns?

The early nonstop departs ATL at 1:35 p.m. and arrives ORD at 2:52 p.m. The evening nonstop leaves at 6:20 p.m. and arrives at 7:38 p.m. From the Sandy Springs restaurant, the airport drive is approximately 35 to 60 minutes outside a major traffic disruption.
Walk through the early one from an 11:00 finish.

You would need to leave the restaurant at about 11:05, go directly to ATL, and target arrival around noon. That gives about 95 minutes before departure if traffic is favorable, but only 60 to 70 minutes if the drive approaches an hour. Any overrun at the site visit would make the 1:35 flight tight. The 6:20 flight gives ample time and would let you stay in the area for lunch or follow-up work.
Give me all four round-trip totals. Regular economy is fine for this comparison.

Current round-trip totals are: Sunday evening outbound with the 1:35 p.m. return, $438; Sunday evening with the 6:20 p.m. return, $402; Monday morning outbound with the 1:35 p.m. return, $386; and Monday morning with the 6:20 p.m. return, $350. All four combinations are nonstop in both directions. Fares can change until ticketed.
So the cheapest is also the one with the better Tuesday margin, but it carries the Monday arrival risk.

Correct. The $350 combination uses the Monday 7:00 a.m. outbound and Tuesday 6:20 p.m. return. It avoids the extra Sunday hotel night and gives plenty of time after the site visit, while the main exposure is a significant Monday morning flight delay before the 1:30 review.
Use that pair for the hotel and transportation comparison. Keep the Sunday 6:10 flight in the notes as the fallback if the lodging math or forecast changes. No purchase.

I’ll carry forward the Monday 7:00 a.m. ORD-ATL nonstop, arriving 10:03 a.m., and the Tuesday 6:20 p.m. ATL-ORD nonstop, arriving 7:38 p.m., at a current total of $350. The Monday review is at 1:30 p.m. near Lenox Square, with an estimated airport-to-Buckhead transfer of 35 to 55 minutes after reaching the pickup area. The Tuesday Sandy Springs visit runs 9:00 to 11:00 a.m.; the evening return leaves ample time afterward. I’ll retain the Sunday 6:10-9:12 p.m. outbound as the $52-higher fallback when paired with the same evening return. Nothing has been booked.
